brief:
Today, 2 November, is Pull A at the New York gym, and tomorrow is Legs A. Nothing was logged on 1 November, so yesterday read as the rest day the last review called fair after four nights in four days; if you did train and the log has not reached the app yet, this review is one night behind and tomorrow’s will read it. Because no new night has been logged, this review repeats yesterday’s: the program is unchanged at version 6 (one dips slot, on Push A; Push B without its dips slot and with the rope pushdown in the overhead slot; Push B 20 sets, Push A 19, chest 18 sets a week), and tonight’s numbers are the ones written yesterday, because nothing new was logged to earn different ones.

Tonight, Pull A, 21 sets, every number in pounds. Deadlift: 235 for 5, four sets (you pulled 235 for 5, 5, 5 at Vancouver on 23 October; tonight adds the fourth set, with the lower back fresh since the RDL was skipped on 30 October, and all four at 6, the top of the range, earns 245). Wide-grip pulldown: 105 for 10, then 120 for 8, 8; this stack is new to you, and your 28 August night at the old home gym was 135 then 150, so if 105 is clearly easy go to 135 and log it. Seated cable row: 105 for 12, four sets; 115 if it is easy. Dumbbell curl: 30 lb for 9, three sets, one rep more than Vancouver, same weight. Cable hammer curl: 35 for 12, three sets. Face pulls: 32.5 for 12 to 15, two sets, up from the 27.5 you did for 15, 15 on 29 October (30 if the stack has it). Cable lateral raise: 10 for 12, two sets, light and strict; this is the slot added on 26 October and tonight is its first night. Stop each set with two or three reps left; this is still week one on these machines. If time runs short (you have never finished more than 19 sets on a Pull A, and Vancouver stopped at three deadlift sets), the order is: the four deadlift sets and the pulldown are not cut; drop the cable lateral raise first, then the second face-pull set, then the fourth row set.

Tomorrow, Legs A: leg press 180 for 10 then 200 for 8, 8; split squat 20 lb for 10 each leg, two sets; leg curl 135 for 10 then 150 for 10, 10; leg extension 150 for 12, two sets; adductor 80 and abductor 60 for 12, two sets each, as starting points (your August home-gym machines took 105 and 135; if these read like that, go there on the first set); calf press on the leg press 250 for 12, three sets; cable crunch 52.5 for 12, three sets. Those are written into tomorrow’s card now, so they are there even if tomorrow morning’s review fails to reach the app; tomorrow’s review re-reads them against tonight. The calf press has been skipped on the last two leg nights (Chennai on 14 October, New York on 30 October), and the decision on it was dated 3 November, the morning after a leg night that has not run yet; by the rule written yesterday it moves to 4 November, the morning after tomorrow’s Legs A. Do it tomorrow, or write in the note what calf machine the gym has instead; it does not go without a replacement.

Two things from the 31 October card still stand. The names you type on a card stick to that slot at this gym: the Legs B squat card reads Leg Extension, the Push B last card reads Overhead db press and the Push A lateral-raise card reads Db lateral raise until you blank the name field. And the two sets you logged as Overhead db press, 50 for 12, 12, stand as logged; the trainer cannot tell from the name whether that was one dumbbell held overhead in both hands (a triceps extension, which fits the slot) or two dumbbells pressed, so on the next Push B write one word in the note, “triceps” or “press”, and the slot becomes the lift you name.

Still open: whether this New York gym is the one you trained at in August (your 29 October pulldown, straight-arm, shrug and face-pull numbers match your 25 August night to the pound, so where it costs nothing the August numbers are quoted as the place to go if a first set is easy; it is not assumed). No bodyweight has been logged since 23 August (207 lb); a morning weigh-in this week would anchor the block.

block.why: Nothing new was logged since the last review: the latest night in the log is still Push B on 31 October, so this review repeats yesterday’s, with the dates moved, and says so. No session was logged on 1 November. That reads as the rest day yesterday’s review called fair after four nights in four days (Push A 28 October, Pull B 29 October, Legs B 30 October, Push B 31 October); if you did train and the log has not reached the app yet, this review is one night behind and tomorrow’s will read it. Meso 3 restarted on 28 October at the New York gym; today is the sixth day of its first week (build to 24 November, deload 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December; the show is 119 days away). The program stays at version 6, written on 1 November: one dips slot, on Push A; Push B without its dips slot and with the rope pushdown in the overhead slot; Push B 20 sets, Push A 19, chest 18 a week. Nothing changes today because no night has been logged since those changes were made, and a change with no new night behind it would be reasoning harder, not evidence. Pull A and Legs A are still the two nights with no New York log: Pull A tonight (the first New York deadlift, 235 for 5 on four sets), Legs A tomorrow, which puts the second leg night four days after the 30 October one. Tonight’s numbers are the ones written yesterday, unchanged, because nothing new was logged to earn different ones. What the week has shown on the lifts that ran stands: every Pull B lift found its rep range on 29 October (the straight-arm pulldown after its first set, 45 for 9, was dropped to 37.5), the leg curl 150 for 10 logged live on 30 October, the shoulder press four sets in range on 31 October. One dated item moves by its own rule: the calves decision was dated 3 November, the morning after a Legs A that has not run yet, and the packet said that if no leg night had run by then the date moves to the morning after it does; so it is now 4 November. The counting-rule question behind nine muscles that read over their ceilings stays dated 9 November, after one full New York rotation; four of the six nights are in. Watched without a date: the Push B reverse pec deck (skipped two of the last three Push B nights), the fourth shrug set, the Push A lateral-raise slot (done as dumbbells on 28 October), the reverse-grip slot (two sets logged as an overhead dumbbell press, read as an overhead dumbbell extension). The next boundary is the deload on 25 November: sets drop to about 60% and each load drops about a fifth, rounded down to the lift’s step, and the prep block is written at the assessment from what these four weeks log.

chest.why: Eighteen direct sets a rotation after the 1 November push-day change (Push A: incline 4, chest press 3, crossover 3, dips 3; Push B: chest press 3, crossover 2), exactly the ceiling of 18 and the same count as before; what moved is that the one dips slot is now on Push A, where you did dips on 28 October, and off Push B, where you refused them on 31 October. Push A is the chest-led night with 13 and Push B the shoulder-led night with 5, on purpose. 10 a week done over four weeks. New York chest nights so far: 28 October (incline 175 for 6, chest press 135 for 12, crossover 12.5 for 12s, typed in from memory) and 31 October (a smith bench 185 for 8, 8, 8 in the dips slot and the high-to-low crossover 29 for 15, 13, logged live; the machine chest press skipped).

front-delts.why: Eight direct sets (incline press 4, Push B shoulder press 4), inside the direct range of 4 to 10; the 15 on paper is those 8 plus half a set from every chest press, both crossovers and the dips, which is the counting question dated 9 November. The shoulder press ran at New York on 31 October: 45 lb dumbbells for 8, 10, 10, 10, four sets in range, logged live, 10 lb under the 25 kg (55 lb) you pressed for 8 and 9 at Chennai on 15 October, so the block opened a step light and has room to climb.

side-delts.why: Eight direct sets a rotation (Push A raise 3, Push B dumbbell raise 3, the Pull A cable raise 2 added on 26 October) plus half credit from the Push B press, 10 on paper, against a floor of 8 direct. 5.1 a week done over four weeks. At New York: the Push A slot ran as dumbbell lateral raises on 28 October (12.5 for 12s, typed in), and the Push B dumbbell raise ran on 31 October, 15 lb for 15, 13, 13, logged live. The Pull A cable raise gets its first night tonight. Watching, not changing, until all three slots have a New York night.

rear-delts.why: Ten direct sets (reverse pec deck 3 and 3, face pulls 2 and 2), inside the direct range of 6 to 12; the 15.5 on paper is half credit from every pulldown and row (dated 9 November). 6.4 a week done over four weeks. The Push A pec deck ran on 28 October, 90 for 13, 12, 12. The Push B pec deck was skipped on 31 October and on 15 October at Chennai, two of the last three Push B nights; in the new Push B it sits fifth of seven on a night that is now 20 sets instead of 23, so it gets one more Push B before it is judged: skipped again and it comes off Push B, and its three sets go to a rear-delt lift chosen that morning from the catalogue, not to a third face-pull set: you wrote on 28 August, when Pull A face pulls were three sets, “Why three? I think two”, and the program cut them to two on 3 September, so that stays.

lats.why: Seventeen direct sets on paper (wide pulldown 3, seated row 4, chest-supported row 4, close pulldown 3, straight-arm 3), 18 with the rollout’s half credit, at the ceiling of 18. 8.5 a week done over four weeks. Pull B ran at New York on 29 October (close pulldown 112.5 for 10 then 127.5 for 9, 9; straight-arm 45 for 9 then 37.5 for 10, 10; chest-supported row 50 for 8s). Pull A gets its first New York night tonight.

upper-back.why: Eight direct sets (seated row 4, chest-supported dumbbell row 4), the floor of the direct range 8 to 16; the 19.5 on paper is half credit from every pulldown, the deadlift, the RDL, both face-pull slots and both reverse pec decks (dated 9 November). 8 a week done over four weeks. The chest-supported row had its first night on 29 October, 50 lb a hand for 8, 8, 8, 8. The seated row runs tonight.

traps.why: Four direct shrug sets planned since 26 October, the direct floor of 4; the rest of the 9.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift, face pulls and lateral raises. The first night of four sets, 29 October, ran three: 80 lb dumbbells for 15, 15, 15. 3.5 a week done over four weeks. No Pull B since, so nothing new: if the next Pull B also stops at three, the fourth set comes off rather than staying on paper.

lower-back.why: No direct slot: the 3.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift (4) and the barbell RDL (3). Held without a direct lift on purpose; a heavy deadlift and a barbell RDL in the same week are the lower-back work. The RDL was skipped on 30 October, so the lower back has had nothing since Vancouver’s deadlift on 23 October and comes to tonight’s deadlift fresh.

biceps.why: Eleven direct sets (dumbbell curl 3, hammer 3, incline curl 2, reverse curl 3), inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 18 on paper adds half a set from each pull (dated 9 November). 8.9 a week done over four weeks. Pull B curls at New York on 29 October: incline curl 25 for 10 then 30 for 9, reverse curl 27.5 then 32.5 for 10, 10, 10. The Pull A curls run tonight.

triceps.why: Eight direct sets after the 1 November change (dips 3 on Push A, rope pushdown 3 and reverse-grip pushdown 2 on Push B), the floor of the direct range 8 to 14, down from 11 because the two overhead-extension slots became dips (which count for chest too) and a rope pushdown, and the Push B dips slot is gone; the 16.5 on paper adds half a set from the incline, two chest presses, the shoulder press and the straight-arm pulldown, which is why it still reads over the ceiling (dated 9 November). 12.3 a week done over four weeks, the best-served muscle in the log by that count, so eight direct sets plus four pressing lifts is enough for now. What you did at New York: dips 8, 10, 12 on 28 October; rope pushdown 42.5 for 12 then 47.5 for 12, 10 on 31 October; and two sets logged as “Overhead db press”, 50 for 12, 12, in the reverse-grip slot, under a name the trainer cannot place on its own (one dumbbell overhead is a triceps extension that fits the slot; two pressed is a second shoulder press), so the next Push B asks you which it was (see that lift).

forearms.why: Six direct sets (hammer and reverse curls), inside the direct range of 2 to 8; the 12 on paper adds half a set from the dumbbell curl, the shrugs, the reverse-grip pushdown and the RDL (dated 9 November). 5.5 a week done over four weeks. Reverse curl 32.5 for 10s on 29 October; the hammer curl runs tonight.

quads.why: Thirteen direct sets a rotation (Legs A press 3, split squat 2, leg extension 2; Legs B smith squat 3, feet-low press 3), inside 10 to 18, unchanged. 3.1 a week done over four weeks, the most under-served muscle in the log, and 30 October was the first quad night since 14 October: leg press 160, 180, 200 for 10, 10, 8 (all three typed in within 12 seconds, so recalled) and leg extension 150, 157.5, 157.5 for 10 in the squat slot because the smith was taken (the first two typed 7 seconds apart). Legs A is tomorrow, 3 November, four days after that night (1 November was a rest day).

hamstrings.why: Thirteen direct sets (deadlift 4, barbell RDL 3, two leg curls 6), inside 8 to 14; the 15.5 on paper adds half credit from the split squat and smith squat (dated 9 November). 6.1 a week done over four weeks. Leg curl at New York on 30 October: 120, 135, 150 for 10, 10, 10, logged live, the first New York hamstring work. The RDL was skipped that night, so the hinge has not run here yet; tonight’s deadlift is the first.

glutes.why: Twelve direct sets (deadlift 4, split squat 2, RDL 3, smith squat 3), inside 6 to 14; the 16 on paper adds half credit from two leg presses and the abductor (dated 9 November). 5.5 a week done over four weeks. Neither the RDL nor the smith squat ran on 30 October (skipped; smith taken), so the only glute work at New York is half credit from the leg press. Tonight’s deadlift and tomorrow’s split squat are the first real glute nights here.

adductors.why: Two direct sets on Legs A, the floor of 2 to 6; the 7.5 on paper adds half credit from the leg presses, smith squat and split squat, which is why it reads over the ceiling (dated 9 November). 1.9 a week done over four weeks. Tomorrow is the first New York night for the adductor machine: 80 for 12 is the starting point from Singapore’s 80 for 15 on 5 October; the August home-gym machine took 105 for 12s on 20 August, and if this stack reads like that, go there on the first set.

abductors.why: Two planned, exactly the floor, all on Legs A. Last 60 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; skipped at Chennai on 14 October. Tomorrow is the first New York night: 60 for 12 is the starting point, the same rule as the adductor (the last machine logged); the August home-gym machine took 135 for 13s on 20 August, so if this stack reads like that, go there on the first set.

calves.why: Six direct sets a rotation (calf press on the leg press, 3 on Legs A and 3 on Legs B), exactly the floor of 6. 1.9 a week done over four weeks, and still no calf work since Singapore on 5 October (290 for 15, 12 then 270 for 14): the Legs B calf press was skipped on 30 October, in a 29-minute night that also skipped the RDL at the start, so this reads as a short night rather than a missing machine. Nothing was logged on 1 November, so the Legs A that carries the slot is tomorrow, 3 November, not today. Yesterday’s packet wrote the branch for exactly this: no leg night by 3 November and the date moves to the morning after it runs. So the decision is now dated 4 November: logged tomorrow and the slot stays on both leg nights; skipped again and it moves earlier in both leg nights or becomes the standing or seated calf machine this gym has, with your note on which exists. It does not go without a replacement.

abs.why: Eight planned (cable crunch 3 and 3, ab wheel rollout 2). 3.3 a week done over four weeks. Both ran on 30 October at New York, logged live: ab wheel 8, 8 from the knees on its first night, cable crunch 52.5 for 12, 10, 10 on this stack. Tomorrow’s Legs A crunch holds 52.5 and chases 12 on all three.

smith-incline-press.why: On 28 October at New York: 155, 175, 175 for 6 each, typed in within 11 seconds at the start of a 10-minute logging window, so remembered, not logged set by set; three sets, not the four asked. No Push A since. Hold 175 for 6 on the next Push A, all four sets, logged as you go; a rep gain on four logged sets earns the next step. The August home-gym incline was also 175 (175 for 8s on 17 August). Whether New York is the gym you trained at in August is still not in the log, so August numbers are quoted, not prescribed.

machine-chest-press.why: First New York night 28 October on Push A: 105, 120, 135 for 12 each, typed in within 11 seconds, so remembered. On 31 October the Push B slot was skipped and a smith bench done in the dips slot instead (185 for 8s), so this press has one New York night on one of its two days. It stays on both: Push A 10 to 12 (hold 135 for 12, three straight sets, logged as you go), Push B 8 to 10 (first New York night still to come; open at 135 and find the 8-to-10 weight). If you would rather the smith bench on Push B, say so in a note and the slot becomes it.

cable-crossover-low-high.why: First New York night: 12.5 for 12, 12, 12 on 28 October, all three typed in within 1.3 seconds, so remembered. Singapore was 10 for 15s on a different stack. Hold 12.5 next Push A and log each set as it is done; 15s on all three earns the next plate on that stack.

machine-lateral-raise.why: In the program since 13 October and never once done as itself: on 28 October the slot ran as dumbbell lateral raises, 12.5 lb for 12, 12, 12 (typed in within 1.3 seconds), and that name now sits on this card at New York until you blank it. Whether the gym has a lateral raise machine is not in the log. If the next Push A is dumbbells again, the slot becomes what you actually do; since Push B already has the dumbbell raise (15 for 15, 13, 13 on 31 October), it would become a cable raise or a different angle, not a duplicate.

reverse-pec-deck.why: Push A on 28 October at New York: 90 for 13, 12, 12, logged live. Push B on 31 October: skipped, as it was at Chennai on 15 October, two of the last three Push B nights (12 October it was 50 kg for 11s). The dossier calls it stalled; that is arithmetic across four gyms’ machines. Hold 90 on Push A and chase 15s. On Push B, now 20 sets with this fifth of seven, it gets one more chance; skipped again and it comes off Push B.

chest-dip.why: In the program since 1 November as the one dips slot, on Push A where you did bar dips on 28 October (8, 10, 12 at bodyweight, in the overhead-extension slot, no note). Earlier bar dips: 10, 10, 10 at Warsaw on 30 September, 8, 8 on 22 September; bench dips ran 17 to 19 at the home gym and Chennai. Three sets of 8 to 12 bar dips, chest lean; next Push A 10, 10, 10, and 12 on all three earns a slower tempo or added weight. This is the catalogue’s bar-dip id, chosen because the old dips id carries the name you typed on it at New York on 31 October (“Smith bench”) and would have shown that name on the Push A card.

assisted-dips.why: Off the program since 1 November: it was the Push B dips slot, and on 31 October you wrote on it that you had two dips cards and did a smith bench press instead, 185 for 8, 8, 8. Its history as dips: 12s at the home gym in July and August, bench dips 15 to 19 on 14 September, bar dips 10s at Warsaw on 30 September, bench dips 17s at Chennai on 12 October, skipped on 15 October. Dips continue on Push A under the bar-dip id.

overhead-cable-triceps.why: Out of the program since 1 November on both push nights. At New York it was never done as itself: dips in the Push A slot on 28 October, a rope pushdown in the Push B slot on 31 October (42.5 for 12, then 47.5 for 12, 10). Before that, skullcrushers on 12 October and an overhead extension at Chennai on 15 October (45 for 13, 15). The last true cable overhead extension was Singapore on 6 October, 115 for 12. Four push nights running the card asked for one lift and got another; the slots become what you do. It comes back if you ask.

deadlift.why: A barbell weighs the same at every gym, so this is the one lift whose numbers compare across the whole log. August: 255 for 6, 6 on 18 August, then 265 for 5, 5 on 28 August. Then 255 for 3s on 20 September (early morning), 225 at Singapore on 8 October (sick), and 235 for 5, 5, 5 at Vancouver on 23 October, three sets, not four. Tonight, the first New York deadlift, with the lower back fresh (the RDL was skipped on 30 October): 235 for 5 on all four sets; all four sets at 6, the top of the range, earn 245, the same rule as every other lift.

lat-pulldown-wide.why: No New York number yet; tonight sets it. Vancouver on 23 October was 105, 110, 120 for 9, 9, 8 on a different stack. On this gym’s stack the close-grip pulldown took 127.5 for 9 on 29 October, and the 28 August home-gym night on this lift was 135 then 150 for 10, 7. Tonight opens at 105 for 10 then 120 for 8, 8; if 105 is clearly easy on this stack, go to 135 and log it.

seated-cable-row-wide.why: No New York number yet; tonight sets it. Vancouver on 23 October was 105 then 115 for 12, 12, 11, 10; the 28 August home-gym night was 105 for 12 on all four sets. Tonight: 105 for 12, four sets, on a stack you have not logged; 115 if it is easy.

db-curl.why: Dumbbells read the same at every gym. 30 lb for 8, 8, 8 at Vancouver on 23 October, the bottom of the 8 to 10 range; 30 for 9s on 28 August. Tonight: 30 lb for 9 on all three, one rep each, not more weight.

cable-hammer-curl.why: Vancouver on 23 October: 37.5 for 10, 10, 10 on a different stack; Singapore 36 for 12s; the 28 August home-gym night 35 for 12s. No New York number yet. Tonight starts at 35 for 12, three sets, a step under Vancouver on a stack you have not logged.

face-pulls.why: 29 October on Pull B at New York, logged live: 27.5 for 15, 15, the top of the 12 to 15 range on both sets, the same 27.5 for 15, 15 as 3 September and 28 August at the home gym; Vancouver’s 22.5 for 14s was a different stack. The dossier’s stall flag is fair: two months at 27.5. Top of the range on both sets earns the step on this stack: tonight 32.5 for 12 to 15, two sets (30 if the stack has it).

cable-lateral-raise.why: Added to Pull A on 26 October; tonight is its first night there. Last run on 8 September at 10 for 12, 13 (gym not recorded); 10 for 13, 13, 10 on 14 August and 13, 12, 11 on 17 August. Tonight: 10 for 12, two sets, light and strict.

leg-press-low.why: First New York night, 30 October on Legs B (10 to 12 range): 160, 180, 200 for 10, 10, 8, all three typed in within 12 seconds, so recalled, not logged live. 200 for 8 was the top of a ramp where the reps fell as the weight rose, so it is not a weight for three straight sets with reps in reserve. Legs A tomorrow (8 to 10), same machine: 180 for 10, then 200 for 8, 8, logged as you go, two to three reps in the tank; three logged sets at 10, the top of the range, earn the next plate. The 20 August home-gym press was 240 for 8. Whether New York is the gym you trained at in August is still not in the log, so August numbers are quoted, not prescribed.

db-bulgarian-split-squat.why: Dumbbells read the same anywhere: 17.5 for 10, 10 at Warsaw on 28 September, 20 for 8, 10 at Chennai on 14 October. Tomorrow: 20 lb, chasing 10 on both legs both sets; 10s on both earns the next dumbbell the rack has.

leg-curl.why: First New York night, 30 October on Legs B: 120, 135, 150 for 10, 10, 10, logged live about two and a half minutes apart. 150 for 10 was the top of that ramp. Legs A tomorrow, four days later: 135 for 10, then 150 for 10, 10, two to three reps in the tank; three logged sets of 12 at 150 earn the next plate this machine has. The 20 August home-gym curl was 142.5 for 13s. Whether New York is the gym you trained at in August is still not in the log, so August numbers are quoted, not prescribed.

leg-extension.why: The New York gym has a leg extension: on 30 October the smith was taken and you did it in the squat slot, 150, 157.5, 157.5 for 10 (the first two typed 7 seconds apart, so recalled; the third logged 107 seconds later). That closes the question dated 6 November a week early, so the slot stays. Tomorrow in its own slot (12 to 15): 150 for 12, two sets. The 20 August home-gym extension was 150 for 13, 13. Whether New York is the gym you trained at in August is still not in the log, so August numbers are quoted, not prescribed.

hip-adductor.why: Last 80 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; 110 for 15 at Warsaw on 28 September; 105 for 12, 12 at the home gym on 20 August, all different machines. Tomorrow sets the New York number: 80 for 12, two sets, as a starting point from the last machine logged; if this stack reads like August, go to 105 on the first set and log it.

hip-abductor.why: Last 60 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; 110 for 15 at Warsaw on 28 September; 135 for 13, 13 at the home gym on 20 August, all different machines. Tomorrow sets the New York number: 60 for 12, two sets, as a starting point by the same rule as the adductor (the last machine logged); if this stack reads like August, go to 135 on the first set and log it.

standing-calf-raise.why: This slot is the calf press on the leg press machine. Done as itself: 300 for 13, 13, 12 on 20 August and 300 for 12s on 16 August (gym not recorded), 290 for 15, 12 then 270 for 14 at Singapore on 5 October. Skipped at Chennai on 14 October and again at New York on 30 October, in a 29-minute Legs B that also skipped the RDL. Tomorrow: 250 for 12, three sets. The August calf press was 300 on a leg press that took 240 for 8 on 20 August; the New York leg press took 200 for 8 on 30 October (recalled, but the only read there is), so 250 is the start and 300 is not quoted; three sets of 15 at 250 earn the next plate. Dated with the calves to 4 November, the morning after tomorrow’s Legs A (1 November was a rest day, so the leg night it waits on moved a day).

cable-crunch.why: First New York night, 30 October: 52.5 for 12, 10, 10, logged live. Singapore was 55 for 12s on 5 October; the home gym 60 for 13s on 20 August. Tomorrow: 52.5 again, 12 on all three; three 12s earns the next plate on this stack.

db-shoulder-press.why: New York on 31 October: 45 lb dumbbells for 8, 10, 10, 10, four sets, logged live. Dumbbells read the same anywhere, and Chennai on 15 October was 25 kg (55 lb) for 8 and 9, so you opened the block 10 lb light and finished three sets at the top of the range. Next Push B: 50 lb for 10 on all four; that earns 55 back.

db-lateral-raise.why: New York on 31 October: 15 lb for 15, 13, 13, logged live. 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) for 10s at Chennai on 12 October; 7 kg for 15s at Warsaw. Hold 15 and chase 15 on all three; that earns the next dumbbell the rack has.

cable-crossover-high-low.why: First New York number, 31 October: 29 for 15, 13, two sets as cut on 29 October. Chennai was 45 kg for 15s on another stack. Hold 29 and chase 15 on both.

rope-pushdown.why: In the program since 1 November, in the Push B slot where you did it on 31 October: 42.5 for 12, then 47.5 for 12, 10, logged live. Three sets of 10 to 12; next Push B 47.5 for 12 on all three, which earns the next plate on that stack.

reverse-grip-pushdown.why: On 31 October you logged this slot as “Overhead db press”, 50 for 12, 12, both sets typed in five seconds apart, fourteen minutes after the last pushdown. Your log is what you did, and it stands as logged. What the trainer cannot tell from it is which lift that name means: two 50 lb dumbbells pressed overhead for 12 twice after four sets of shoulder press with 45s would be a second shoulder press on a triceps slot; one 50 lb dumbbell held overhead in both hands for 12 is an overhead dumbbell triceps extension and fits the slot. The slot is not changed on two recalled sets from one night.
